qc.label_under_test: The 'as' (or the 'a' just after it) when me, us or you is labelled back: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, thinking of, regarding, treating, describing or hailing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group see, think of, regard, treat, describe or hail me, us or you 'as' something in return; the return can end in a noun or an adjective. Weaker but can still fire: the same two-way mirror written entirely with third-person pronouns (he and her, they and him). Weak: mirrors between named people or noun phrases (the coach and the striker), a return clause aimed at a third person after an earlier clause about me, us or you, a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause, me labelled first and then answering back, the bare form without 'as' even inside a mirror (thinks me a fool), a return framed as what someone should do, and official appointments to a post.

neighbours.label: The 'as', or the 'a' right after me, us or you, when a label bounces back at me, us or you: an earlier clause has me, us or you seeing, calling, regarding, treating or describing someone else as something, and a following clause has that other person or group label me, us or you in return, either with 'as' (they saw me as a fool) or bare with 'a' (he called me a liar). Weaker: the same two-way swap between named people or third-person pronouns. Weak: a one-way label of me, us or you with no earlier clause; me labelled first and then answering back; a plural bare return with no 'as' or 'a' (named us cowards); a return aimed at a third party; official appointments to a post.
fire: I always saw him as a mentor, but it turned out he saw me as a rival.
I called him a coward, and he immediately called me a liar.
We treated them as guests, yet they treated us as intruders.
You regard her as a genius, but she regards you as a nuisance.
I thought of the old man as a stranger, while he thought of me as a grandson.
We described the neighbors as friendly, and they described us as noisy.
She called you a hero, and you called her a saint, so I guess you saw her as an equal.
I viewed the coach as a tyrant; he viewed me as a lazy kid.
quiet: I always saw him as a mentor, and he taught me everything about carpentry.
I called him a coward, and then I walked out of the room.
We treated them as guests and served dinner on the good plates.
You regard her as a genius, and her paintings sell for a fortune.
I thought of the old man as a stranger until he told me his story.
We described the neighbors as friendly in our letter to the landlord.
She called the firefighter a hero, and the newspaper printed her words.
I viewed the coach as a tyrant, so I quit the team in October.
